NoteTexAccessor::packages¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch NoteTexAccessor::packages() const

Inventory Package Dependencies Per Cell¶

packages() extracts package names from complete \usepackage, \RequirePackage, and \RequirePackageWithOptions declarations. A declaration that names several comma-separated packages contributes one trimmed token per package. This makes the result a package inventory rather than an inventory of raw argument strings.

An optional argument may appear between the command and required package group. Balanced brackets inside that option are consumed as part of the declaration and do not become tokens. The required braced group is balanced too. Empty comma fields are ignored, declaration and package order are stable, and duplicates are retained because repeated declarations can carry different options or document-local significance.

Matching uses exact control words. \usepackages is not \usepackage, a doubled backslash is an escaped command boundary, and a declaration without a complete required group contributes nothing. The method does not load files, resolve package installations, merge options, inspect included documents, or decide whether a package is available.

The result is ragged: tokens() is one flat Text Note and offsets() is an Int64 Note with one boundary per receiver cell plus the final boundary. Cell i owns [offsets[i], offsets[i + 1]). Higher-rank receivers are traversed in row-major lane order. Tokens own their strings. Undefined input produces undefined tokens with offsets [0]; defined non-Text input is rejected.

Scanning is linear in source bytes plus copied package-name bytes. It performs balanced delimiter scans but does not construct a TeX syntax tree.

Example 1: Options, Lists, And Declaration Forms¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\usepackage[margin={1in,2in}]{geometry, xcolor})",
    R"(\RequirePackage {amsmath} \RequirePackageWithOptions{hyperref})",
    R"(\\usepackage{escaped} \usepackages{long} \usepackage{, })"});
const auto result = source.tex().packages();

std::cout << result.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["geometry", "xcolor", "amsmath", "hyperref"]

The comma inside the balanced option does not split the package list. The escaped command, longer control word, and empty list contribute nothing.

Example 2: Recover Declaration Ownership¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = result.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 2, 4, 4]

The first two cells each declare two packages; the boundary-only third range is empty.

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Input¶

const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined().tex().packages();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << absent.tokens().defined() << " offsets=["
          << absent.offsets().integers()[0] << "]\n";
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).tex().packages();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "packages Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false offsets=[0]
packages Int64: rejected
